summary: The note examines a series of late-2023 telecommunication outages, including an October 15 cyber-attack in the Northeast and a November 22 weather-related outage in the Midwest, and asks what role government should play in ensuring network reliability. It covers expert and industry views on redundancy, cybersecurity, public-private collaboration, disaster preparedness and user-centric regulation. It concludes with the proposed Directive on Network Integration and Reliability (DNIR) of January 5, 2024 and a call for continuously evolving policy.
one_line: Following 2023 cyber-attack and weather outages, the note discusses how governments can strengthen telecom reliability, including the proposed DNIR directive of January 5, 2024.
key_facts: On October 15, 2023, a major service provider's network in the Northeast suffered a crippling cyber-attack.
Mary Sutherland, a telehealth service provider, said the October 15 outage disrupts real-time health consultations with serious implications for patient care.
On November 22, a vast swath of the Midwest lost power due to severe weather, causing prolonged internet and telecommunication failures.
Julian Barnes manages a library affected by the November 22 outage; he said the library relies on internet connectivity for cataloging, resource management and serving the community.

Dr. Helen Zhao, a Telecommunications Policy Researcher at the National Institute of Technology Management, says policymakers must work closely with technology experts and industry leaders and emphasize resilience and rapid recovery alongside prevention.
Dr. Helen Zhao argues regulatory frameworks should mandate multiple pathways for telecommunication signals, likened to building various roads between two cities.
Sarah Gibson, an FCC spokesperson, said the commission is working with cybersecurity experts to devise strategies to prepare the telecom industry for attacks.
Larry Johnson, CEO of a major telecom company, said industry brings innovation and implementation while government provides a strategic framework guided by national interest and public safety.
After the November 22 outage, several legislators called for more stringent requirements for backup power solutions and physical fortification of critical telecommunication assets.
The note says government can protect consumers by enforcing service level agreements and penalties for excessive downtime.
The government proposed the Directive on Network Integration and Reliability (DNIR) on January 5, 2024 to integrate stakeholders' efforts into a cohesive strategy for high network reliability.
Regulators often play catch-up with innovations like 5G, fiber optics and satellite internet because technology evolves faster than policy.
